overview: This two-page file index summarizes correspondence and interdepartmental communications concerning Japanese tonnage dues and port-entry rules from 1937–1938. Its principal subjects are Japan’s tolerance of the USS GOLD STAR carrying private commercial freight between Japan and Guam without paying ordinary dues; the eventual Navy Department order limiting the vessel to government cargo; the requirement that ships stopping at Yokohama enter and clear the port even without handling cargo; an inquiry involving the SS TEXAS; and an earlier Japanese Embassy request for information about American practice regarding entry into unopened ports.

subfiles.title: List of papers, sheet 1: tonnage dues and naval cargo, entries 1–6
subfiles.from: U.S. Department of State, compiler not named
subfiles.about: An index sheet records correspondence on unopened ports, Japanese tonnage dues, the USS GOLD STAR’s carriage of commercial cargo, and the SS TEXAS at Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: The sheet begins with a Japanese Embassy inquiry about American practice in permitting ships to enter unopened ports and the charges imposed there and at open ports. Most entries concern the USS GOLD STAR’s transportation of private cargo from Japan to Guam, which Japan had tolerated without ordinary tonnage dues, and the Embassy’s view that the vessel should either pay commercial dues or stop carrying private freight. Further entries address the Japanese requirement that ships stopping at Yokohama enter and clear regardless of cargo operations, as well as a Commerce Department inquiry into whether the SS TEXAS loaded or unloaded cargo there.

subfiles.title: List of papers, sheet 2: resolution of the USS GOLD STAR issue
subfiles.doc_type: list of papers / file index continuation
subfiles.from: U.S. Department of State, compiler not named
subfiles.about: The continuation sheet indexes the Navy Department’s decision to restrict the USS GOLD STAR to government cargo between Guam and Japan.
subfiles.summary: The sheet records a Navy Department communication of February 4, 1938, describing two possible procedures for settling the tonnage-dues issue. It states that the Navy had directed the USS GOLD STAR to carry only government cargo to and from Japan. A February 9 entry records the transmission of that decision to the American mission in Japan.

interest: The index is useful for reconstructing a small but revealing dispute at the boundary between naval logistics and commercial shipping. It shows how a U.S. naval vessel’s carriage of private cargo created questions about Japanese taxation, port formalities, and sovereign privilege, and it documents the administrative solution of restricting the ship to government freight. The references to the GOLD STAR and TEXAS also provide leads to correspondence that may illuminate everyday enforcement of Japanese maritime law in the late 1930s.
